review_text:
In times of crisis, this is the place to go. I've had two dogs treated here: one a senior dog and one a seemingly healthy Labrador.

The senior dog began having severe health problems due to a heart murmur and seizures. There were a couple times we almost lost him and they brought him back and then monitored him over several days - giving us frequent updates. With medication and close monitoring, they extended his life past his life expectancy and we are so grateful for the dedicated care.

Our 5 year old (very healthy) Labrador began foaming at the mouth and vomiting blood. We were able to get her seen RIGHT away - which can be critical in these situations. They were very thorough - they even checked for chest and abdominal sensitivity as well as her temperature - all of which were abnormal. But that's how thorough they are. 

When pets are family, choose a vet that will treat them like family.

I am writing this review to warn other pet owners about the aggressive scare selling tactics, lack of direct communication with the actual veterinarian, and questionable diagnostic pressuring at Tri City Vet. Last week, I brought my cat here for the first time because they were close by. My cat was weaker, eating less, and had vomited once three days prior. After a brief 5-10 minute talk with the vet prior to the examination (owners are not allowed to go inside with their pets), the assistant came out, told me the condition could urgently deteriorate, and presented a $1,200 package for X-rays, blood work, and a Cerenia injection. Everything moved incredibly fast. Shockingly, after that initial brief meeting, the doctor never spoke to us again. Instead, they used assistants to relay everything. When I hesitated, the assistants told me that if I wasn't willing to do the X-ray, the doctor said he wouldn't feel comfortable treating my cat at all. Feeling backed into a corner, I proceeded with the $1,200 package.An hour later, the medical assistant called us in to discuss the results. She began by using the wrong pet's name and proceeded to tell me my cat had cancer. I had to correct her because she was reading the wrong file! After finding the right file, she told me there was a "linear obstruction" and quoted me $3,000 for surgery the next day, or $10,000 for emergency surgery that night. When I showed hesitation, I was met with high-pressure statements about how critical and dire my cat's condition was, and how his condition was actively deteriorating.I then asked for the X-rays and the radiologist's report. They only sent the text report, not the actual images. Crucially, the radiologist never confirmed a linear object. The report actually stated they SUSPECTED enteritis OR a linear object, explicitly noting a lack of many indicators that corresponds to linear object. In fact, the radiologist's report specifically noted that there were small opacities (gas) but NO plication (weird folding) or abnormal enlargement of the intestine. The next day, another assistant called and asked, "Are you sure you don't want to proceed with surgery? There is a string stuck inside your cat." Again, I had to correct their staff right away and read the radiologist's exact words back to them. The assistants here are entirely too comfortable throwing around diagnoses with absolute certainty when the specialist never confirmed them. The radiologist also noted that if the condition worsened, an ultrasound should be done to rule out a string or linear object. When I asked Tri City about ultrasound availability, the assistant told me their traveling tech wouldn't be available for a few weeks. That's when it clicked: if the only way to for sure confirm a string inside was an ultrasound, and they didn't have an ultrasound technician available for weeks, they expected me to just blindly agree to a $3,000 invasive surgery to open up my cat's stomach--potentially for absolutely nothing, leaving me with a massive bill and a recovery process for a surgery he didn't need. Thankfully, I trusted my gut. My cat's condition improved drastically overnight. By the next day, he was already eating solid food again and is doing great. I am incredibly thankful I did not let this clinic scare and pressure me into an unnecessary, expensive surgery. Please be careful, trust your instincts, and always ask to read your pet's actual medical reports if you come here.

I know how stressful it is when your animal needs care, so I feel obligated to share what happened to me in the hope that others can avoid the same ordeal. This is my own experience as a client here, and it came down to three things: prepaid services I never received, repeated billing errors on my account, and a near-total inability to reach anyone who could help.

The prepaid plan I purchased. I bought their "Kitty Premium" plan that was offered to my 9-months old kitty, which included a second appointment. I was never given that appointment, and I have not been refunded for the unused portion of what I paid.

What happened with my billing. I was double-charged. The front desk staff told me the account manager would sort it out, but the account manager never returned my calls or texts. After weeks of back-and-forth with nothing resolved, I ended up opening a dispute through my bank to get the charge corrected. When someone from their team finally did respond to me, the figures they gave me were wrong. And they finally make the correct refund.

Where it went after my dispute. Once the bank resolved the charge and paid them the correct package amount, I was still not given the second appointment I had already paid for. That left me opening a second dispute simply to recover money for a service I never received. I am still in an unresolved back-and-forth with them over it.

My experience trying to reach them. Getting hold of anyone with actual authority was, for me, extremely difficult. My calls and emails rarely got a response. Their text line is staffed by an outsourced help desk that could book appointments but told me it had no access to billing or account information, so every attempt I made to resolve the double-charge stalled there. Messages I asked to have passed to the account manager went unanswered. The only thing that ever got me a reply was a credit card dispute -- and even my own bank had difficulty reaching them. Being routed to a channel that could not help me, with no path to someone who could, turned what should have been a simple billing correction into weeks of wasted effort.

Where I stand now. I have emailed their office a document titled "Settlement Proposal: Dispute Resolution & Refund Request for Kitty Premium Package," laying out a clear path to settle the balance and part ways. I will keep this review updated as things progress, and I will revise it if and when the matter is resolved.

Bottom line: Based on my own experience, I would not recommend this practice. Save yourself the trouble and take your pet elsewhere.

First off, they charge you an examination fee even if you're only there for a quick deworming. Fine, I treated it as a standard consultation fee. Afterward, the vet came back out to explain that one of my cats had inflamed gums and prescribed antibiotics. Just for that basic visit, the deworming, and the antibiotics, it already cost me over $300. But it isn't the worst part.

​About a week later, that cat started sneezing. Since he was already on antibiotics for inflamed gums, it cleared up in a few days, so I shrugged it off as a temporary allergy. But a week after that, my other cat started showing the exact same symptoms--except hers got worse, and I had to take her to a different vet. Turns out it was an Upper Respiratory Infection (URI). My cats are 100% indoors and never go out. 

Connecting the dots, the only place they could have caught this virus was at this clinic.
​I was actually planning to schedule the tooth removal surgery with them, but after this? Absolutely no way. Avoid this place if you care about your pets.

As a concerned pet owner, I feel obligated to share my experience to help ensure others do not face similar issues. We are hardworking individuals trying to give our pets the best care we can afford, but the events we encountered at Tricity Veterinary Hospital have raised serious concerns.

Issue 1: Billing and Record Keeping Errors
We contacted Tricity Veterinary Hospital to schedule a routine dental cleaning for our first dog. The receptionist informed us there was a credit of $519.17 on file, which had been noted by the bookkeeper. After asking them to verify the credit, they confirmed it was due to an overpayment, so we scheduled a cleaning for our second dog as well. The appointment was set for October 17. 

On October 20, we were contacted and told there had been a record-keeping error, and that we owed $519.17. We explained that we wouldn't have scheduled the second cleaning had the credit not been available. Despite our multiple requests for confirmation, the staff continued to assert that the credit was from an overpayment and even suggested a payment plan, blaming the issue on a "system glitch."

We had signed an agreement for services totaling $699.50, with the noted credit. It is concerning that this error might not be isolated, potentially affecting other customers. It's critical that Tricity Veterinary Hospital reviews its billing practices to prevent other pet owners from relying on inaccurate information and facing unexpected charges due to "record-keeping errors."

Issue 2: Dog Mix Up for Medication Inquiry
The second issue involved a call from staff notifying us that our dogs were denied the Sentinel Spectrum flea and heartworm prevention medication due to a history of seizures, which our dogs do not have. When we asked the administrator to double-check, she refused to do so at first and continued explaining, claiming the denial was based on our dogs' history. Only after we insisted did she review the records and realize she had confused our dogs with another pet. This lack of attention to detail is deeply troubling and raises concerns about the reliability of their medical records.

Issue 3: Lack of Accountability from Dr. Shiv Salwan
When we asked the staff and bookkeeping team to take responsibility for the billing error, they refused and pressured us to resolve the issue by making the payment. We requested a call from Dr. Shiv Salwan, hoping for understanding and resolution. However, Dr. Shiv did not apologize. He explained that another dog with the same name as ours was mistakenly linked to our account but continued to insist that we were legally liable to pay the full amount for the second cleaning.Dr. Shiv also used the example, "If the bank deposited $10,000 in your account, would you question it?" We responded that we had already asked his staff several times to verify the credit and check the records, trusting that their records were accurate. At that point, we had done all we could as clients. Dr. Shiv remained dismissive, suggesting we should have done more, and continued to push us to resolve the matter without taking responsibility for the mistake. In the end, Dr. Shiv suggested that we "go our separate ways."

We are deeply disappointed with this experience. What was once a well-run veterinary hospital now displays a lack of professionalism, accountability, and care for its clients. I worry that other pet owners may face similar issues without proper resolution.

My pup was experiencing some orthopedic issues, likely related to a previous surgery (not done by this vet), and I was having trouble finding a vet in the area that could see her quickly. They were able to see her same day when most vets were booked a couple weeks out - in hindsight, perhaps this was a red flag instead of a whisper of hope.

I arrived at 11:25a for my 11:30a appointment. Three employees behind the desk, but not a glance or a welcome. No worries. I stood there, patiently, for 10 minutes until someone asked me what I needed.

I met with the vet, he suggested x-rays, I understood and signed off. He said her injury was in or around the knee, but wouldn't know more until scans were done. We opted to do them same day and would pick her up later. They took her back to start the prep, and I asked if I could see her before she was sedated (you never know). They agreed, told me to wait out front, but came back a few minutes later and said it was too late and I couldn't see her. I wasn't allowed to go back and she couldn't be brought up front.

We were told that they'd call us when she could be picked up, likely around 5p (7p closing). At 6:30p, no call. So we called, and they say, "yes, she's ready for pickup." Of course she is. It was probably hours ago. The following evening, we get a call from an employee to go over the results. We're told that there's *nothing* they can do, and that "in the meantime" we should make her "comfortable" with "pain management, weight reduction, and reduced activity." This is a young, active dog with an orthopedic injury - does this language seem appropriate? These are phrases you use for terminal patients.

I had many questions, in terms of next steps, what the specific injury was, what we should do... "I'll have to follow up with the doctor." No prognosis, no forward thinking, no recommendations. I asked if I could sit down or speak with the vet on the phone, and I was told, "that's not possible, he's very busy, but you can book another exam and bring her back in." At this point, I haven't seen the scans, I haven't spoken with a doctor, but I'm being told my dog can take drugs and lay down moving forward. I asked what the actual diagnosis was, and I was told, explicitly, "that her bones are all out of normal position, and the hip is nothing like he's ever seen before" and that "surgery is not an option." We cried the rest of the night.

Over the next week or so, I fought with them to get her records and her images. We're now two weeks out and I STILL do not have the scans, just pictures of the pictures, despite repeated requests. I ended up bringing her to another vet, had to pay for additional x-rays (because the previous ones weren't taken with her hips in the right position and were paper copies, difficult to use) and put her through another round of sedatives and physical exam.

I spent 1.5+ hours with this new vet, getting x-rays done and reviewing immediately after (all at one appointment), received an actual prognosis, multiple recommendations, and formed a plan. The experience was night and day, and I'm absolutely furious that I gave this Tricity a single dollar. I've already contacted a lawyer to discuss options, as nobody should ever have to be put through an experience like this again. I'm sure this vet can handle tummy aches and vaccines, but I would never recommend you bring an animal with a serious issue. From the moment they saw my pup, or at least after x-rays, they should have said that they weren't capable of assisting, and that surgery wasn't something *THEY* could do, based on their expertise and the specific issue at hand.
Oh, here comes the best part - the new vet did the physical exam with me (unlike Tricity, who took her from me), and walked me through each step, including findings. Turns out the knee is fine, as is the alignment of bones.

TL;DR - Worst experience I've ever had at a vet. Incompetent, disgusting behaviors. Before I paid? Nice, friendly, quick to respond. After paying? Won't answer calls, doesn't respond to emails, won't send our records, didn't send proper documents to vet through referral. Complete shift in attitude once they realized they weren't capable of helping and we wouldn't be paying them for anything else. However, they had no problem offering for me to pay for another exam to go over the x-rays that I already paid for (and still don't have).

review_text:
I was with tri city for 3 years (since my dog was a puppy) and in the beginning it was ok/decent. I tried to give them the benefit of the doubt because they are relatively cheaper than other places, but over time things got increasingly worse. On one occasion, my dog was diagnosed with IVDD and the next time I came in to see a different vet, they said she had no symptoms of it...I felt like I was being lied to. My dog was terrified of this place and I couldn't help but think of the bad treatment she was getting when I was not there.

The employees here are more than likely overworked and the place is short staffed and not ran well which is why there are so many horror stories about people and their pets. I have a new vet now which is completely worth it. Avoid this place at all costs, seriously. If you're still here you should find a new vet. I don't know how this place hasn't shut down yet.

Took in a cat who had escaped and then come back. Wanted to check health, he was very skinny. They took him in within 48h. Once there, they were slow to evaluate. Insisted to take him for IV fluids so he could get tested. Were told we'd get tests back within 48h. We are 2 weeks later and 4 calls in, and have not gotten test results back. They say the doctor is out at lunch no matter what time of the day it is, you're on hold for 20min, and no call back. Avoid like the plague. They take your money and don't give you information.

if i could give zero starts i would. I started going here in 2014 and since then they've brought me and my family nothing but despair. They charge for things your animal doesn't need, and try to temporarily fix the issue so you keep going back to put money in their pockets. The miscommunication sucks and i feel like they never hear my concern or try to fix it. I understand this place charges a lot less than others, i have 7 cats and a dog so i understand why people come here. But every time i try to save money and come here they create bigger issues and i end up having to spend more money going to my expensive( but we'll educated and amazing) doctor so he can fix their mistakes. This place only makes you take half a step forward and then 10 steps back. if you love your pet, spend the extra hundred and take them to a vet who actually cares about them healing and their well being. i'm never trying to use a shortcut and come to this cheap place again. GARBAGE!!!!!

After several years of subpar service, overpriced procedures and supplements, and mix ups with appointments and scheduling shots, I'm finally done. I'm shocked they've even achieved a 2 star average. This practice is a joke, they lack any semblance of professionalism and upsell/overcharge when they can. Go to Central Vet Hospital. 

Shame on you for running a business like this, Dr Salwan.

My dog is being treated for cushings disease.  He was prescribed Vetoryl 10mg for 30 days.  I purchased a box of 30, but after about 1 1/2 weeks I noticed he did not have enough to finish the 30 days.  I realized the box was 10 pills short.  I did not want to go through the hassle of debating the number of pills they sold me, so I just went in to purchase another box of 30.  Before purchasing, I double checked that it had the correct number of pills, which it did.  When I was preparing to give him the first pill from this box, I noticed the pill was bigger.  The label TriCity placed on the box said it was 10mg, BUT the box and cards inside said it was 120mg!!!!!  Had I not caught this, it would potentially killed him!  Then, because of this, my dog was off the medication for over 1 week and I had to start his 30 day period of treatment over again.  It took 5 phone calls and 2 more visits to the clinic to finally get a refund for the wrong pills.



What type of Vet Clinic is so careless with dispersing of prescription medication?  How many other pet's lives are they putting in danger due to these types of stupid errors?  The pills they dispense are not normally in a box from the manufacturer, so who knows what you are getting/paying for in those generic bottles?


Aside from just this example, they are always very disorganized. Depending upon which Vet you see (they have 2), you can get 2 different diagnosis and recommendations.  Both give you the impression that they really don't care about animals, but just want to make a buck.


When I took my dog in for one of his Cushings test, I knew I had to leave him for 3 hrs to complete the test, so I told them I would be back in 3.5 hrs (knowing they are always running behind).  Within 1 hour, I received a call that my dog was ready to pick up!  I knew it couldn't be right, so I came back at the time I stated. When I arrived, 3.5hrs later, they said they were not done and I had to wait another 30 minutes.  On 2 occasions prior to this, I arrived for his Cushings test appointments, but they neglected to order the serum required to administer the test, so I had reschedule.


They are ALWAYS over booked and wait time, with an appointment, is 30-60 minutes.  If you have blood work done, they tell you they will call when results are in, but this never happens.  You have to call after a few days and they will email you the lab results and tell you the doctor will call you, which also never happens.  You either need to call back and stay on hold until they are available or go into the office and wait to see him.


Walking into this place you get the feeling you are in a Covid breading ground! Proper mask usage is not enforced.  Customers and staff are wearing masks under their nose or below their mouth over their chin.  I had to tell one of the office assistance standing next to me that her mask was not doing any good over her chin, so she fixed it. There is no extra cleaning of counters or frequent touch points. No sanitizer is available to use after you touch the same counter that everyone else has been touching all day.


Needless to say, I have changed Vets!  If you care about you pets health, and your own, do not go near this place!!!!

This place is terrible. This is the worst experience I've ever had at any veterinary. I had an appointment at 3 and wasn't out of here until 4:50ish. When I mentioned to the assistant that the doctor didn't come talk to me she said "oh it's okay, I'll tell you what you need to know". They tested my dog for parvovirus there and told me it was negative. Once I'm checking out the lady at first desk asks me "do you remember how much he weight because they forgot to write it down". They sent me home with medication and a stool test to bring back the following day. I received a call at 10am saying that my dogs stool didn't have any parasites. How did they know if my dog didn't have any parasites if I hadn't dropped off the stool sample yet?? I came in to talk to the doctors and the front desk said they couldn't talk to me because they were "busy". There was one girl at the front desk who was truly trying to help me figure out what was going on. There was just so much confusion going on. 

I received my dogs medical record where it says he's 5M which he's not at the time he was 6-7 weeks. The notes on his chart that I received say my dog is 12M & 2 weeks. This place has no idea what they are doing!

I took my dog his own food when he stayed four days overnight at the boarding, his food was a full bag and when I received it back from them it was nearly empty. I know my dog will not eat a whole bag of dog food in four days. It's really disappointing they charge people 5 dollars a day to feed their pets but when owners bring their pet's food they feed it to other dogs. It's just very unprofessional!

I've been taking my dog to this place since I got her 8 years ago. Every single time I would take her in they always have issues pulling up her records. I've told them multiple times to put my phone number on her file and they never did. The last time I took her was back in June. We had an appointment and we came a little early. When I came in they acted like I was brand new (again). It wasn't until after they made me fill out a new client form that they were able to find my dog's record. They had me wait in the exam room while they took my dog somewhere else for the vet to look at her. They didn't explain why at all, but I let it go cause I figured it was due to COVID. They had me waiting for over an hour! No one came in to update me on what was going on. I could hear the 2 receptionist talking and complaining about people they were talking to on the phone. They called one lady a bitch. I also overheard them take a walk-in and had that person dealt with while I was still waiting! The room was gross; it was dusty and sticky. When I made they appointment I said my dog needed her vaccines and had other concerns. When they gave me a summary of what they could do I asked why the vaccines were left out. The technician had no clue what I was talking about, then she said since they were already doing other stuff to my dog that I should come back later. Fast forward to today: I found a new vet for my dog. I called tri-city so I could have my dog's files. I called around 3:30 the girl that answered said no problem I'll email them to you. I waited over 2 hours and no email. I called back and was put on hold for over 20 min. Hung up and called again; and was placed on hold for another 20 min. I waited awhile and when I called I got the busy signal. After 7 I finally got someone on the phone! I explained my situation and I still didn't have my let's records. She kept asking for my email address because she kept messing it up and in the back ground I could hear the other receptionist tell " Just have her come in!" This place has gone super downhill. I'm never going back. Their receptionist are rude and have no idea what customer service is. Avoid this place.

We at the Ohlone Humane Society are so grateful for Tri City Veterinary Hospital to take on our foster kittens for sickness and spay/neuter surgeries last year in spite of the pandemic.  It was/is extremely busy there all the time; they are open more than any other vet office usually is let alone during the shelter in place and the shortage of vets in the Tri City area so sometimes you may have to wait.  Ask when you make the appt for the slower time to help avoid that but if you or others have an urgent need, they will get you in.  Be prepared with questions and take notes, get names of the staff and vets and get to know them.  We were able to take into foster over 330 kittens last year and all but 5 have gone to forever homes.  Thank you Dr. Salwan,  Dr. Bhullar and all of your staff for everything you did to help make this possible. We couldn't have done this without your support.

My bichon, Meemee, has been getting vaccinated here before it was tri city veterinarian hospital. They get the job done when it comes to vaccinations, however, time management here is my gripe on the business. It takes over an hour just for an exam and one vaccination. They seem fairly staffed so I'm not too sure if it's management not prioritizing, or if their computers and software are outdated, or if they are taking their time on things. It would be nice if they would let the people know coming in, that they are aware of their presence and verbally express that they will get to them shortly.

Also, calling for surgery appointment is near impossible. I was put on hold twice for two days, but I'm a patient person. I just came by the hospital again and spoke to them in person. 

Their puppy packages (year long vaccinations) are well priced at under $150.

Update: you have to catch them at an early time for them to get back to you quickly on your questions and concerns. I'm glad that the techs/receptionists got back to me shortly after my concern over my dogs pain medication. Their prompt service like this makes me feel a lot better.

review_text:
I see a lot of horrible reviews about this place which I just don't understand! Since the first time I came in here, I was impressed by the looks of the office. Real clean and organized, fell in love with the cute paintings of animals all over the place! I have been there many times and I personally have met the receptionist, vet techs, and doctors and they are all wonderful people! Friendly and welcoming.

Another important aspect would be the prices, and no not because it's cheap its bad. They are the same vaccinations and treatments you get anywhere else. I was also impressed by their Puppy/Kitten packages which are designed to save you money. It comes with vaccinations and services that your animal will need, they combine it into one to have you bundle and save. Instead of paying one per one and have the costs add up. 

Great place! My pet always come out happy, they do care about your pets! Changing their name is not the only change they have made. TriCity Vet has also changed staff and overall trying to find better ways to IMPROVE! Give this place a chance, see it for yourself,  instead of listening to outdated reviews.

Get. Your. Shit. Together. 
Went in to bring my sister's dog in for a neck scrape. The only real reason we went here is because they were accepting new patients and it was kind of an emergency. 
Got in, didn't even get checked in until 20 minutes later. 
They said he needed to a skin scrape and needed medication for it. No big deal. We left him with the vet because it was going to take about an hour or so. We went to run errands. When my sister and I got back to the clinic, I gave her my card and told her just ask for the receipt while I waited in the car. A few minutes later, she comes back with her dog saying they didn't charge her nor did they give her his meds. WTF? They had previously given us a break down of the charges along with medication and now, nothing? So I told her to wait in the car while I go double check. After a routine checkup and a recommended $400 ex-ray from Dr. Salwan, my rabbit DIED the same night. I really want to warn all pet owners never to bring or trust their animals in the hands of Dr. Salwan and his employees. But after the death of my rabbit, how they handled this entire situation was completely heartless, unprofessional, and guilty.  Go here for time and dates on what happened: https://www.facebook.com/thewantedpickle/posts/10212987948520679. 
My aunt brought our rabbit in for a checkup and Dr. Salwan suggested that she get an ex-ray. After the ex-ray Dr. Salwan said it was a hairball as he suspected. He never told my aunt there was any risk involved with ex-rays nor did he say this hairball was life threatening. 
The rest of that day, Neffy couldn't walk or even stand up straight. I called them around 9pm and the receptionist said there are no doctors available and she couldn't answer my questions. I completely understand that. I asked if she could please call Dr. Salwan. She said she will. She called back and said the doctor said this behavior is very normal after getting 2 doses of injections for the ex-ray. On the receipt: "injections for a 0-25lb animal," when Neffy was only 5 lbs. To me 2 doses for a rabbit, seemed really high. I didn't question it because I believe a vet knows what he is talking about. I asked her if she is 100% sure this is normal, and she said totally fine. I trusted them! And at 3 am, Neffy died. I was so shocked and in disbelief. This rabbit was to help my disabled aunt and give her a sense of purpose and the fact that something she loved so much died for no reason, is just horrible.
I went to TriCity Vet the next morning to tell them what happened and ask why?  The receptionist said, "Not to sound insensitive, but what do you want me to do." I told her, "I know this is not your fault, but I need you to please have Dr. Salwan call me and tell me what happened to my rabbit." She refused tell me when Dr. Salwan would be in. I don't know her name, but she is short, white, blond long straight hair, and really rude and insensitive.
That night, I went in. I asked the receptionist on duty if I could speak to a doctor, she went into another room and came out saying sorry they are unavailable. This receptionist was really nice and printed out the conclusion from the exray,  which we never received initially. 
That night I wrote a review on TriCity Veterinary's Facebook page (which now has 2.4 stars). 15 minutes after my review, I get a response from them saying that they told me the rabbit died of gastric stasis syndrome. We have never heard of the term gastric stasis. When I looked at the ex-ray conclusion, it clearly states "Gastric Stasis syndrome is a primary RULE OUT." I responded to them asking "how has the diagnosis changed and why hasn't a doctor told me this, but you can say this on Facebook." (They have since deleted their lies on my review, but I have screenshots). 
Everyday we called and went in asking to speak to Dr. Salwan and nobody would let us. I finally I called to make an appointment with Dr. Salwan.
The day of the appointment, I walk in and immediately the technician, Aly, recognizes me. I said I have an appointment with Dr. Salwan. She tells me "actually he was called out for an emergency" and immediately puts me in a room. This has never happened, where I have been put in a room immediately. I honestly believe they wanted a chance to warn him to leave, so I couldn't see him. Another doctor comes in, and with all my questions he repeats, since he is not the doctor that worked with the rabbit nor is he a rabbit specialist, he couldn't answer my questions. I point out that on Facebook, I was told she died of gastric stasis but on the conclusion it clearly states "rule out." This doctor has the audacity to say "rule out" means she has it.... What?! And while he talks, he goes, "sorry, do you understand what I am saying?" Treating me like I am stupid. Aly was there too. She says, "you guys made the choice to give her an exray and not everybody takes the doctor's recommendation". I am sorry, when a doctor doesn't explain any risks involved and highly recommends an exray, as loving pet owners, we say yes. It's only a risk when you do NOT take the doctor's recommendation. Because she stated this, it makes me ask again... did Neffy die from the ex-ray procedure or from gastric stasis? These people are just lying every second and will not give us a straight answer, while Dr. Salwan, the man responsible, has completely disappeared. 
Please, please you can't trust these people with your loved pets. They are unknowledgeable, money-hungry, and guilty people who don't care about animals and refused to tell you what is going on with your pet. You can see from their 2 stars and many reviews that people's pets have randomly DIED with no explanation.  This was a really sad and heartbreaking experience that was really handled dishonestly by these people.

He told us that this could be caused by constipation, or maybe even a hairball. Dr. Salwan recommended an x-ray to get a better conclusion of what was going on with Neffy. My aunt agreed to follow his recommendation. Now, at no point during Dr. Salwan's talk with us did he mention how the x-ray would work. We got lunch, and then returned after 2 hours and wait for Neffy in the front office. We patiently waited before we ask the receptionist for an update of Neffy and her x-rays. On December 19, no one called me all day so I CALLED AGAIN I was already upset at this time (because it's been almost 2 months) they said the ashes was ready to be picked up. How are you gonna tell me that you don't provide that service when your employee Maricar told me that she spoke to someone and she was told it was being made separately?! So basically they were lying to me the whole time. Did they think that I'm stupid and I'd forget? Of all places and of all people they should know how important our pets are to us. Alyssa kept on telling me that she would give me a refund. What she doesn't seem to get is It's not about the money. It's the fact that they lied over and over again. If they were honest and told me that they didn't provide those services I would I taken our dog elsewhere. They can not turn back time and Un-cremate our dog. Dear pet lovers, you can go any vet places but not this one. I went there for my new puppy first exam and met with the doctor Raj Salwan. " It's a love & hate relationship " @ this place but I still love coming because it's super close to my house lol & because the staff are supper nice. They might get a little busy @ times & get a little frustrated because people are a little impatient but other then that I really love this place & the Veterinarians are great nice people that are trying to help you & your pets 
I honestly give this place a 5star review because they do get there job done  even if they are low on staff. THANK YOU ALL FOR BEING SO GREAT & TAKING CARE OF OUR BABYS(pets)

Today was a hard day... we had been planning to take our Portuguese Water Dog in for his final appointment at TriCity Vets, as the Vet from Allcare Vets in San Jose was working there... and our Arnold was in a lot of pain. We followed the instructions, and when I called in to confirm that we were on our way I was told that although they were busy they could fit us in. However, the price we had been told was considerably more by the team in San Jose. Same owner, but honestly... that wasn't the problem.

When you are saying goodbye to a family member, who cares about a few extra dollars to get it right. However, the attitude that I encountered... the attitude that "we are already doing you a favor by fitting you in" and "if you don't like the price we charge you should talk to the people in San Jose"... again, same owner... but they aren't "affiliated".

Had the person on the phone been more sensitive we would have simply driven out to Fremont... but she was not! Such lack of compassion not just angered me, but put our entire family into a situation where we had to find another vet at short notice. Why, you might ask? The thought of having my family, who was already in a tough spot, experience such insensitivity during a traumatic moment like this was one that I didn't want to experiment with.

We lost our dog and family member today... but if and when we need to get our next furry companion in for a Vet visit we will NEVER return to Allcare or TriCity! EVER!!!

I was a VERY happy patron when Dr. Liao was still in San Jose... now, not so much. A sad day made just a little worse, thanks to these guys!!!

DO NOT GO HERE! The Vets are money hungry and they will try to drain as much $ out of you as possible without any real consultation. 

I took my maltipoo puppy here when she started limping and whining about a pain that was located in her left knee. 

Immediately, without any proper consultation or exam, the Vet told me that my puppy has luxative paella. Which I almost admired since it feels like she knew her stuff. She then went on and demanded an x-ray from us, which was fine since I wouldn't want my baby to take any meds nor get treated for something that she doesn't precisely have. 

After what seems like the longest x-ray ever, the Vet came out and immediately informed me that the surgery for the luxative paella would be $2200 & that she already called the surgeon whom will be available in the next 2 days. 

First of all, I AM grateful for their quick turnaround , but she didn't even allow me to swallow in what was going on with my puppy nor gave me time to ask any  further questions before she forced the surgery on us, and deliberately called the surgeon without our consent. I mean, is there another option for this treatment? This isn't a quick 5 mins treatment she was suggesting on my baby. It's SURGERY! 

I asked for another option & she kept turning them down claiming that none would work nor would be helpful for my puppy. 

From my understanding, I know dogs with luxative paella can't be "cured" with meds or vitamins, but i'm sure there ARE other ways to potentially help (i read on the condition while I was waiting for the vet to come out with my baby during her x-ray). My puppy was only 1 year old btw. 

After i refused to go through with the surgery without seeking for other options, the Vet finally opted for anti-inflammatory so the pain can stop. 

Not having any trust in her at all, I immediately booked a exam with the Banfield Veterinary Hospital & got a much better &helpful exam  for my puppy. They were patience in answering all of my questions & concerns. Plus, I was right! With rest & proper meds, my pup could potential recover from the pain & the surgery can wait til later. 

Never ever ever going back here again.

After more than 2 weeks we still did not recieve anything. When i called again they told me about this new policy of a closing fee for my records! Are you guys really that terrible of a clinic that you have to enforce a new fee if people are unsatisfied with your service and wish to leave? Wow. 

If you just take a second and look at the other yelp reviews it is pretty sad that this place is even still in business. Then again they did change thier name from American Animal Hospital, which i highly suggest you look up. In thier parking lot they didnt even bother to change the parking signs which still says their old name. The wait time is way too long. The staff is always suspiciously changing. I just cant trust this place anymore. I love my dogs way too much to subject them to this practice. Im sure they do okay work on thier patients but just okay is not good enough for me.

The next day came and he looked worse so I rushed him to Beacon were they said his liver was enlarged and prescribed him Baytril (liver antibiotics) and more Cerenia. After about 10 days he started to recover but we noticed there was a lump where Tri City inserted the fluids it started to harden around the lump and it never dissipated. Three days ago the skin around it broke and started to Ooze. I made an apt. with Newark Pet Clinic and they said it was due to NON STERILE FLUID TUBES and is now a huge infection! I went ahead and had them drain the abscess' and they prescribed me different antibiotics for this now. I am NEVER EVER EVER taking any of my dogs to this vet clinic again (Tri City Vet). Terrible place! Newark Pet Clinic did a Great job with getting rid of the infection and my dog is finally able to begin healing. 2. Inefficient staff! I always make sure to get a copy of service done coz they forget to chart the vaccines. Inaccurate records delay boarding care or prohibits day care.

Now, how can I have my dog vaccinated in another clinic if they don't release the records on time? As dog parents, we have the right to our dogs medical record anytime!

The doctors do not take your time with your pet, they rush you and are in-sensitive. Normally do not spend more than a couple minutes with your dog before they rush out of the room only to leave you stranded for another 20 minutes until they deliver your bill.

This was my first appointment at this facility. The wait time to check in for an appointment was ridiculously long. At least the receptionists were nice and apologized for the wait time (the only reason I gave two stars). I'm not sure why it took an additional hour to get my cat vaccinated (I was informed it would only take about 15 minutes).

The veterinarian was not friendly or welcoming at all. I don't even know his name since he didn't bother introducing himself. He was condescending for the most part, and he didn't even remotely seem interested in my cat's medical history. I just wish this vet could be a little more compassionate and caring (or at least pretend) when he's examining his furry patients.

I strongly recommend you visit another practice. If you do come here, be prepared to wait a LENGTHY time for unsatisfactory service.

These people are just after your money . Spent hundreds of dollars still were not able to cure the dog . Took it to a different vet started showing signs of turn around the same day at the fraction of the cost . 
-20 stars

Way way less expensive than our regular vet who wanted is to take him 1 1/2 hours away to a dentist and he is terrified of the car so we went to Tri City for a second opinion. Have to wait and see if it works but at least he was thinking of Jack and looking for  alternative treatment instead of pulling his teeth which is a big expense. He clearly was thinking about his well bring instead making money. And the visit cost a fraction of what we normally pay even with an injection. So glad we went there. it was the first time our dog came here. Picked it for the reviews and the price. I deducted a star because the last vet place we went to in Milpitas when my pups peed on the floor the vet made it seem like it was no big deal and cleaned it up for me... this place didn't even offer napkins... but that really isn't a big deal - it's my dog.

They neutered him and gave him shots and were thorough with the info. The office section part of it looked like it needed at least a few good hours of straight devoted time for organizing. 

I made a payment the night before and the next day they didn't see it and had to search for it again. once the lady looked it up in the system she found it. I wasn't going to pay twice.

Rates are reasonable - staff is friendly. Milpitas was friendlier and seemed like they loved my poopy more than this spot. My poopy is easy to love! jk I will take him back here..........

If I could leave zero stars, I would.
Two incidents, both negative experiences. 

First, a kitten who had a tumor in one ear that needed removing. Surgery at Tri City Vet Hospital left her with stitching scars that deformed her (they were poorly done), she had blood all over her face when I picked her up post-surgery, and she sneezed blood for days after the surgery (a sign her nostrils hadn't been cleaned out and the wound properly packed to prevent blood draining into the nasal cavity). I ended up taking her to another vet to get the post-op care she needed, because I didn't trust Tri City to do right by her after that.

Didn't learn my lesson from that; assumed this group would have improved. Not the case at all.

Second, my cat died. Had Tri City Vet Hospital perform the euthanization (he had massive renal failure). It was late at night. We paid over $300 for the euthanization and cremation/box services for him. Was told 2 weeks they would call us to let us know to pick up the ashes. Two weeks pass - no word. I call. "We'll have someone call you back." No one called. Three weeks pass - no word. I call. Twice. Leave two messages. Am told someone will call me back. No word. Four weeks - no word. I call, irate. Am told it wasn't 2 weeks, but 4 weeks for this service (no apologies were made for this mistaken information given to me). I ask where the ashes are - still aren't in. I become irate, demand they take action. No one calls me back. I call again, get the manager's voice mail. Demand she take action and call me back. No call back. I call her later that day and demand an update. "Miraculously" the ashes are available (I'm now suspicious that they aren't my cat's ashes at all, but that this group screwed up and dumped his body that same night they euthanized him. I believe they might be lying about having cremated him at all, and am going to look into how much it costs to test bone fragments, which are typically left behind during creation, for residual DNA for my cat just to see if they are, in fact, his ashes), but there was something wrong with the name tag (supposedly), so they'd need to send the box back to the crematorium to get it fixed. Am promised a call when it's ready. Another week passes. No call. I call them, irate again, and demand they give me my cat's ashes and that Dr. Salwan call me, himself, to discuss. Manager calls instead, says she drove to the crematorium to get the box herself and it's ready for pick up. I pick up the box a few days later (due to personal issues interfering). The name plate is wrong. The box is poorly constructed (the bottom screws are screwed in wrong and sticking out - a cutting hazard for hands). The presentation is cheap, tacky, and I demand they fix it. Days go by, no word. I call them, irate again, demanding Dr. Salwan call me. Manager tells me he doesn't talk to customers, implying I have to go through her (who has done a terrible job at customer service thus far). I demand she get my cat's box fixed - a better presentation for what I paid, a correct name plate. I threaten to contact my lawyer and the State Vet Board about this. She says it'll be done. A few days pass - no word. I call them AGAIN. Manager gives me a song and dance about how it's still not ready, but they won't be giving me a better box ("it was made for you"). What a bunch of B.S. I inform her I'll be contacting my lawyer, contacting the State Vet Board to complain, contacting the Fremont Argus about investigating them for possible fraud, incompetence, and poor customer service, and leaving this negative Yelp about it. Manager seemed unfazed by any of it. More empty promises made of getting the box to me, but no time frame allotted. No promise of a call back this time, though, I noticed.

No surprise the Manager of this facility wasn't even bothered with the threats of legal action or reporting to higher authority, since looking at all of the negative Yelp reviews of this place, it's clear they don't care how unprofessional they are, or about correcting their negative reputation with the community. 

I would never recommend Tri City Vet Hospital in Fremont, CA for any reason to anyone. In my opinion, their actions have proven that they are incompetent, unprofessional, and totally lacking in any compassion for customers who are dealing with sick animals, or their remains after they have passed.

I have a love hate relationship with this place. 

The manager Francesca is awesome! So sweet and always remembers your animals names. 

The main issues I have with this place is inconstancy & time. Almost every time i've called to get information about something and confirmed if i was to come right away that would be honored, when I get there it's like whoever was talking to me on the phone doesn't exist. 

Every time I've been here theres been many new faces, not a problem to me but it just seems that their employees never seem to be consistent for me to build a relationship with other than the manager Francesca. 

When it comes to time it seems like they don't care if you have other obligations. I've come for my dog's appointments a few times to be sitting there for over an hour just to be seen by the doctor. I get it, vets can be busy but maybe its an issue with over scheduling? It's just a little frustrating when I come in for just a check up, literally a visit that can take up to 10 minutes or less with the exam to be there for over an hour waiting just to be seen. 

I appreciate the fact that they now carry Bravecto! I'm not too sure how I'm liking the medication but I do now I really enjoyed nexgaurd when my dog was taking that an this seems to be a better alternative since it lasts longer!

review_text:
I am a resident of Fremont, CA for the past 12 years and have been bringing my pets to Tricity for the entire duration.

On May 3rd, I visited Tricity Veterinary Hospital located at Fremont, 37177 Fremont Blvd, Fremont, CA 94536.

The owner Dr. Raj Salwan treated my dog Ruby (Goldendoodle) who had severe swelling, bleeding and pus in her rear left foot. The owner and Vet Dr. Salwan personally treated her and said that the likely cause was a fox-tail and that he needed to operate her, keep her under observation the entire day and then release her. I picked up Ruby in the evening the same day. The release papers did not say anything whether he was able to retrieve the fox-tail or not or whether she was operated. There were essentially no notes written up by him on what was done as part of the surgery and if the cause on infection was addressed by Dr. Salwan and Tricity. 

For the next 3 weeks Ruby suffered with continued swelling, bleeding and pus oozing from her foot and her wound did not heal. So finally I brought her back to Tri-City where one of the Hospital's technicians looked at Ruby's foot and said that the Fox-tail was never removed. He took less than five minutes to remove the fox-tail (without anesthesia or needing to hospitalize her like it was done by Raj Salwan) and in the next 24 hours the swelling, bleeding and pus was gone. She is perfectly fine now.

In the first visit I was charged $400+ and the second visit I was charged $227.  Dr. Salwan not only over-charged me by recommending false hospitalization for something that required 5 mins and no anesthesia) but also did nothing to treat my dog, left no notes saying that the fox-tail was never retrieved. He requested an unnecessary procedure, did not treat it and overcharged me where his own technician was able to remove the fox-tail for less half the price, no surgery and in less than five minutes. 

My dog and I suffered for 3 weeks due to this gross negligence, fraudulent and unprofessional behavior. Please do not take your pet there.
review_photo_captions: Fox-tail that was supposed to have been removed the first time.
Ruby's foot 2 weeks after surgery performed by Tri City.

review_text: Scamsters. Our dog had a surgery scheduled on Saturday to remove his bladder stones. When we arrived, the doctor is not interested to perform the surgery saying the quote they provided maybe incorrect. They wanted to perform more test for $400. We agreed and made the payment but haven't received a call for 3 days now. We were promised the vet would call us for sure the next day before we made the payment. We called 4 times so far and vet wouldn't talk. This place is just a scam and should be investigated and shut down. Please stay away.

I'm giving them a one star because I did not have a good experience at this veterinarian clinic first of all the wait was way too long I got to the clinic at 2:30 and didn't get out until 5pm. We came in for a swollen foot and the doctor tried to say that my dog could possibly need surgery for her uterus because her stomach is large and she was bleeding from her vagina and I let them know that she's just overweight and is on her period because she's not spayed yet. They are money hungry you can tell. It would of cost over $ 500.00 just for blood test and X-ray. They have Terrible wait time and horrible customer service. Please don't take your dog here unless want to be gouged for money and you want to wait several hours just to be seen and just to be checked out. Horrible place !!!!!!!!!!!!!! Horrible service!!! Ps. They told us to spray her medication behind her ear what??!! and when we went back in to clarify, they said the label was printed wrong, was missed printed and it's supposed to go on the foot. This place is aweful !!!!

Great service every time. 

The staff is extremely friendly. They don't bombard you with stupid monthly emails like most places. And when you make an appointment they text you ONCE the day before to remind you. 

Even though it's a hospital it doesn't seem that way nor does it smell like one either.  

Love this place.

We brought our puppy here since our regular vet was closed, and they had an appt available. 

When we entered, no one greeted us. Something smelled weird in there. I'm not sure whether it was from a lack of cleanliness or the food products they had in a nearby room. We just waited by the front desk waiting to be given new patient paperwork. The woman working didn't really acknowledge us, and later we realized that we should sign the sign-in sheet and wait. The wait was about a half hour before we were able to be seated into a room. 

When the same woman left the room that she seated us in, she slammed the door closed each time she left. Very unnerving since my puppy was already scared to be in a new environment (us too honestly), and loud door slams don't really help anyone get comfortable. The veterinarian was a nice man (sorry didn't get his name). His assistant was also very kind. The vet administered the vaccine we came for and described follow-up care.

Again, we waited and waited for the receptionist woman - only so we could pay for our vet visit. She went from working on the computer, to calling new appointments in, and weighing animals - all while we stood there in front of the front desk waiting to pay. 

The front desk staff was horrible. The veterinarian and vet assistants were kind and knowledgeable. This vet has a room of dog/cat food and treats in a connecting room, which seems convenient. Looks like they also have boarding. There was a beautiful husky in the boarding room when we went. Poor thing seemed alone and neglected the whole time.

FOR THE SAKE OF YOUR BELOVED PET, PLEASE BEWARE AND TAKE THE FOLLOWING REVIEWS TO HEART. IT'S LONG, BUT PLEASE READ. YOUR PETS LIFE DEPENDS ON IT.
Our dog is not alive anymore, we had to go to another emergency vet due to heart failure, and 20 minutes after walking in, we had to put him down. He passed away from cancer, which yes, would have happened anyway, BUT, the care, if you want to call it that, was very slow in coming at TriCity. 
Everything is wrong with this place, except Dr. Bhullar, who did his very best with the tools available to him.
Calling for an appt.? Good luck if they even answer, and then you're put on hold forever; you hang up, same thing happens, until you call back a third time and plead for them not to put you on hold, because you already were twice before. Read the reviews...so many complaints about that. The place is dirty and smells of urine. The treatment room looks dirty and is a disaster. Our Dr. is so over-booked, that there isn't time to clean anything or sanitize before the next patient is taken back. That includes the front counter where you check in and out.
If you're waiting for lab results, even if the results are bringing you the worst news possible, you might want to call yourself for results, because they didn't find it important enough to give us a call; they don't have enough staff to do their jobs efficiently). 
We came in on a Monday, still not having a "final" diagnosis of cancer, but to drain a mass to relieve pressure, and were told to bring our dog back on Thursday for an MRI.
We showed up Thursday, and were told their MRI machine was broken; no one called us, and furthermore, our vet had not been told it wasn't working. 
They knew how sick our dog was, getting weaker by the day, peeing blood, abdomen so bloated, no appetite, etc.
That was on a Friday; the Dr. gave us the name of a specialist in Dublin, but he wasn't going to be in the office until early Saturday morning.(He had been off for several days).
Unfortunately, we couldn't wait until Saturday morning; had to take him in late Friday night; he was in heart failure.
Whoever owns/runs this place is a money grubbing scumbag, and could care less about his employees and certainly not about our precious pets. 
The delay in our dog's diagnosis increased his suffering by at least 3 days.
PLEASE DO NOT GO HERE IF YOU CARE ABOUT YOUR PETS.
By the way, we were told our records would be sent over to them asap, but when we arrived, they had only sent a partial record; this new vet knew right away that the lab results indicated cancer; labs that had been done 6 days prior along with x-rays.
TriCity has been getting negative reviews for many years now; they need to be shut down!!!
Next stop, Better Business Bureau.

The last straw was recently when my dog came in for a pain near his neck. The doctor said that we should do a blood test to see if he had pancreatitis again and that he would provide the results and talk to us about the results. However after a few days we weren't given a call or any information. When we did call they said that they would do it but they just fazed over a blurry photo of the results. After this we had the credit card stop the payment as they never returned our call or cared to contact us after we had already paid to see if he had pancreatitis and if so what we needed to do for treatment. Right after that they called us back to "see how he was doing?" They called back a week after that and said that they messed up and should have called us and wanted to see our dog. We tried again and it was even worse as they said they gave him fluids and to come in the next day to do more fluids. When we came the next day they weren't even aware that we were asked to come in. Then when he came back they said the doctor was too busy to go over the results and that we needed to make an appointment to do that when they had told us to come in and the doctor had said he would be there to talk about our dog with us. We left and went to another vet as our dog was still in bad shape and we needed to make sure he was okay. The next vet was very professional and helpful and found that under the bandage was the catheter that Tri-City was supposed to remove when they gave our dog back. So they were the ones to remove it and finish the job that Tri-City should have done. There have been numerous problems with this place. A majority of the front staff are rude and are terrible at communicating. There have been a few times where they have forgotten to give us medication. Other times they've charged us or forgotten to charge us. And they've given us medication and paperwork for another dog. To top that off they are extremely rude. They act as though customers and the pets coming in are nuisances however they are more than happy to take your money. The doctors try to get you in and out as quickly as possible and 9/10 will not meet with you and will answer the bare minimum of questions that you may have. There have been enough bad experiences here that the list goes on. I urge anyone thinking about coming here to please reconsider as this is truly a horrible place for animals. The staff here is truly heartless and the care here us dangerous for the pets coming in. For those who decide that they want to try it regardless, I just advise you to keep good records of what is being done and try to get as much information as you can beforehand as so many problems with treatment plans occur at Tri-City.

I have worked in a veterinary hospital before. I know poor management, training, and practice when I see it. 
Receptionists are innocent, but horrible. Terrible customer service, not well trained or organized. Even before COVID-19, this place has been a mess. There isn't enough staff to support the amount of clients the hospital services. 
I recently took my pup's stool there to be sent out for fecal testing. After two days with no results follow-up, I called to check in about his results. They put me on hold saying they were going to go speak with the Doctor about the results, and then hung up. I called again, then they said the doctor wasn't in? At 2pm on a Tuesday? After just saying they were going to go speak with him? Ridiculous.
 I called back the next morning, they said they would call me back. Nothing. 
I called a final time the next morning and Annie, one of the receptionists informed me that "everything went right on their end" but the testing lab didnt have any results for his routine fecal test. This was 5 days after the test was sent out. I was doing all the calling and checking-in, the staff weren't even aware that the lab hadn't sent in any results for my pup yet. This hospital can't even keep track of their own clients. 

In addition, the place smells and is dirty. Dr. Salwan's father ran the vet hospital before him. It used to be an okay place. review_text: I brought my senior 16 year old dog here after being told by her previous vet that it was time to let her go. Not only did they take her in the same day, but the vet was very knowledgeable and clearly explained why there was still hope for my dog. You would think that after saving my dog's life by preventing me from ending it too soon, the total bill would be high. I called in to make an appointment for my bird's eye injury as they are the only clinic in Fremont that can see birds. Over the phone I was only asked about my information and nothing about the pet in question, or what he was coming in for. A little weird, I thought, but went through and made an afternoon appointment that day.

I get there and the place is empty. There were two receptionists who ask me to fill out paperwork and as is standard procedure, I comply. Everything is extremely disorganized and the two staff members that I saw were not prioritizing their tasks very well (customers waiting to pay! Calls on the line! The usual). I am standing there for about 20 minutes until a tech comes out from the back to hand another client some meds; she sees my bird cage and goes "uuuuuh we don't have a bird doctor today". The receptionist turns around to me and says "you're gonna have to reschedule to the weekend, sorry, I didn't know". 
As this was an eye injury which means -urgent because the bird can go blind!-, I asked them if there are any other doctors or clinics nearby that sees birds. All three shrug and say something along the lines of "naw, maybe Berkeley". Avian vets are rare so most places would have a list of alternatives to take birds to. Closest one that came to mind was Castro Valley Companion (where I would have taken the bird to, but their avian vet only works on select days; this happened on his off day) and Santa Clara Pet Hospital (I couldn't fit a trip to the South Bay that day so that was why I chose Tri-City)... but no mention of these two places. 
I ask the receptionist what time was available and she replies "any is ok. How about 10". She doesn't seem to write or take note of this, so I ask for a confirmation call or email. Her reply was "ok", again with no intention of making note of this.

I walked out, felt unsure because my bird can go blind now and I wasted my time waiting for this appointment instead of driving out to Santa Clara. So I called my old boss (an avian Vet) and asked her for some first aid advice, walked over to Hallers Pharmacy (thank you Hallers in my time of need!!!) and picked up some saline to irrigate his eyes. Then I made an appointment at Santa Clara for the next day, and canceled my appointment with Tricity.

I was livid. Birds are prey animals that hide injury and illness very well, and small amounts of blood loss can have grave consequences; any sort of injury needs to be seen as soon as possible to stomp out complications. The staff didn't seem to care, and that sort of attitude comes from the top. The lack of consideration, empathy, organization, and overall professionalism of the front house staff speaks volumes. In the end I didn't see the doctor here, but what I had experienced during my thirty minutes there was enough to tell me that my money was better spent elsewhere.

PS we took the bird to Santa Clara Pet Hospital this morning and he's ok now.

We put him on carnivore care, reptaid, and reptaboost. The day of the appointment we were able to bring over a fresh fecal sample to have tested. The front desk seemed nice, we saw Dr. Salwan they couldn't weigh him which made me think they probably don't see very small animals too frequently. The doctor checked inside his mouth for mouth rot and his heart beat. We told him what we were doing to get him back to health and he took some notes. He couldn't estimate how old our bearded dragon was, which made me think that he probably didn't see bearded dragons too often. We went ahead and did a fecal exam to check for parasites. 

While we were waiting to pay, a couple came by requesting results from their dog's exam/test, they were angry that they were told they would hear by now, and it's been too long, they wanted the results today and they weren't going to leave... Yikes! The lady at the front desk showed no empathy and didn't apologize at all... The exam was $33.50 and the fecal test was 66.50, $100 total. 

My problem with this place is that they have one he'll of a front to collect your money. But to get what you pay for is like pulling teeth. Our exam was on Saturday, the exam test results should have came in 2 or 3 days, but we didn't get a call on day three, so we waited a day, still nothing. I missed their call on Thursday because I was at work, no voice-mail was left. So I called back when I got off, and the guy who answered the phone said that the doctor will be in tomorrow and will call again, I told him I don't want to miss the call again so can I request a time for him to call me? He told me he was still in, but in a room and he'll call after which will be 30 minutes, an hour later, still nothing. I called back and a lady answered, told me that the doctor the guy on the phone earlier was referring to wasn't the reptile doctor who saw our bearded dragon and that he'll call me on Saturday from 12pm to 2pm. (I know this is his lunch hour because I asked for this time frame for our first exam.) 

Saturday comes, it's been a week and guess what? My boyfriend and I probably called this place 4 times so get our results for our bearded dragon and on separate phone calls they put us on hold for about 6 minutes, they told us the doctor would call us back, and during out last call they told us that the doctor was just about to call us, and we should hear from him in 10 minutes. We received nothinggggg. 

On Sunday evening, day 8 I finally get a call, from a doctor that we didn't even see about the results of our bearded dragon and suggested we come by and pick up antibiotics that'll be around $40.

I don't recommend this place to anyone, I see why they have so few stars for a rating. The people here don't care about their clients, and neither do the doctors. Seems like they only care about collecting money. In 8 days time a pet can die from parasites depending on the strain especially if they aren't eating and are dehydrated, I'm glad we were able to nurture our baby back to a healthy state without their help, if we relied on this horrible place he definitely would have died.

Had an appt last week on Thursday to see the doctor for a regular dog exam at 7 p.m. I even called around 5.30ish to confirm the appt. And then when we reach there at 7 pm with the dog, we were told that the dr left! We were like, what? If the dr had to leave for whatever reason, why could the front staff not call and reschedule our appts? What incompetent staff and dr!

And then we take another appt and go to see dr for a regular pet exam and a shot and they made us wait for an hour to just do something that takes perhaps 20 mins max. Hence just 1 star!

This place needs to be shut down.  I was actually warned about their bad practices before coming here by two different shelter employees, but decided to give them a chance despite all the negative reviews.  Also because their prices on services and medications are so much lower than everywhere else (I wonder why?).  The receptionists here are so rude and unfriendly, they don't even pretend to care about you or your animals.
I brought my male puppy here to get neutered and good thing he got out of there alive.  his wound and stitches looked so choppy and infected we were worried about the work they did the entire time it was healing.  It healed up but still the skin is bubbly and it will never be a clean scar. 
My puppy has worms right now, and I have been trying to get a de-wormer for him for several weeks from this place.  Every single person I talk to at Tri City Vet has different information, it's like they change the rules EVERY SINGLE DAY.  The first lady told me that she would get a prescription from the doctor and call me back to come get it, and of course they never called.  A week later a different girl told me to come in after 2 pm and they would give my dog the first dose and we would do the 2nd at home, we came in and waited forever for someone to help us but NOPE.  So we left.  The third call was today and the receptionist very rudely told me that they won't give any dog a de-wormer without testing their feces, it's not safe for the dog to give them possibly incorrect medicine.  I brought in my female puppy to get a de-wormer a month ago, she even saw the doctor and they gave her the pill without doing any testing or checking or knowing what type of worms she had.  Now they won't give me a pill for my male puppy, and they are baffled as to why the doctor would have given my female the pill without testing her first.  What?!  Are these even licensed veterinarians? I ask them why they gave my dog the pill without testing or checking her, and they don't have an answer.  I ask them which doctor it was and what his name is, they don't know.  Is this a joke?  Never bringing either of my dogs here again and if you love your animals you won't either.  It is not worth the risk and bad care given by the doctors and staff.

Great place, great staff.  I have been bringing by bulldog, Bentley, here for years for both boarding and exams.   I have never once had a problem with the team at Tri City Veterinary Hospital and I would refer friends and family as well.  No complaints from my side....

First visit my puppy was seen I was not given enough info. The next day my puppy was not doing well and found worms I was told  there was nothing they could do until her next de worming visit in two Weeks. Mind u my puppy is only 6Weeks old was having diarreah and not eating.
Called another vet she was treated right away with med. All in the same day. Not happy with the excuses I was given.

I am beyond upset and furious with this place! NEVER TAKE ANY PET HERE! 

I brought my 5 month old puppy here for boarding for one day, she was spayed last week and I could not leave her alone, especially for the amount of time I would be gone. We were asked to bring her food, her toys and blankets to make her night there more comfortable. They also said to bring any treats she might like. We were assured she would not be around any other dogs since she still had her cone on and was not supposed to be super active. When I dropped her off at noon on Dec. 24, the lady there at the front desk wasn't mean, but she definitely didn't look like she liked her job. When we called that morning to confirm that our puppy was okay to come, they informed us she had to be looked at by a Vet to check her and make sure it was okay for her to stay there, which is fine. They put us on hold though for 15 min, and came back and said their vet was out. We had already made this appointment for her last week to stay there and they knew she had to be seen, so why would they not have a vet?! She put us on hold again for 20 min. So we had to hang up and call back, she said " Oh, the vet should be here by noon" so we said fine. So when we got there I filled out her paperwork, and they took my puppy back to get checked. I went to grab all her things from the car, when I cam back with it, the lady asked for me to show her the food, so I showed her everything. What treats needed to be at what time, and her servings of food. She assured me everything would be fine. When I went to pick her up this morning, there was a young man at the front desk, he went to get my puppy, and when he brought her,  he asked what I had brought with her, I found that a bit odd because her blankets and toys should have been in the same kennel with her, shouldn't it? Well I told him anyways, like 10 min later he comes back with her stuff. I said thank you and asked if I needed any paperwork to sign her out, he said no, which I found odd, because you would think they would want to make sure the pet goes home with the correct owner. Anyways, as I get to the car I started to look through her bag. NONE OF HER STUFF WAS TOUCHED! THEY DID NOT FEED HER HER FOOD! I was furious. None of her food was eaten, all her toys and blankets were exactly as I left it. I went straight back in there and said " did you guys not feed her?! None of her food is touched." The young man was like, "uhm, give me one sec, let me go check" he walks to the back,  and when he comes back, he said oh, we fed her our own vet food. I said that was unacceptable!  They told us to bring her food, and second, you do not give someone's pet food without permission! I have no idea if they really even fed her or what they fed her! They did not give her a specific treat for her teeth. I am beyond furious with this place, I will never take my puppy here again. I will be reporting this place. It's beyond unacceptable how they handled everything. 


My poor baby probably hadn't eaten in over 24 hours. 

I repeat NEVER TAKE YOUR PET HERE! not if you care about them. 

This place should have NO STARS!

The reason for my 1 star is because the vet did not make me feel at ease. He was not very friendly and did not seem like he enjoyed what he was doing. Had us wait for an hour and made us come out to ask someone else...We complained about the bill later and demanded that we take our dog home instead of paying for the overnight charge. When we brought our dog back home, they didn't even bother taking the bandage and IV fluid attachment off him. We had to do it ourselves. 

Definitely not coming back here. Disorganized, lack of communication, and some may think this place is "cheap" but we were nearly juped for an extra $204 dollars. I also have a friend who loves his dog dearly. He took his dog here and they squeezed $4500 out of him. I read that this place is "cheap" and to be honest, if it truly is as cheap as some people say it is, then I can see why this place sucks so much.

This review is largely due to the poor front office and supporting staff members. I came in just to get shots for my cat and flea medications, yet I ended up being there for over an hour. I felt uneasy with this office as soon as the technician walked in to administer the vaccines and asked that I hold my pet. Most vets that I have been to will have another tech hold the pet while another administers the medication. I asked her why she is having me do it and expressed that I did not feel comfortable with doing that, so she grabbed someone from the back who CLEARLY was not a tech. It took the tech several tries to administer the shot, even with the assistance of someone else. My cat had a HORRIBLE experience. I don't believe this tech was very experienced!!! 

When the receptionist was tasked with writing a prescription for Revolution for Dr. Sangha to sign, she wrote the date wrong, MISSPELLED my cat's name and even wrote the WRONG breed! I can't believe how incompetent she could be! When I brought this to to her attention, she said both the misspelled name and breed were information that she had found in the system. Whoever typed my pet's new patient forms couldn't even type any of her information correctly. She then attempted to draft a new prescription, yet spelled the breed's name wrong! I have never felt so dumbfounded in my life. I gave up at this point and decided I would later use 1800petmeds to send Dr. Sangha a request for the prescription, a step that I later realized was e a mistake. The majority of this appointment was spent simply waiting for the front desk staff to do their job. 

Needless to say, I will NEVER, EVER bring my pet back to this hospital. I could never trust them to do any procedure on my pet, basic or not. I am just glad I didn't bring my cat in for a more serious cause. Please do not make the same mistake that I have made by ordering medications from an 1800petmeds  in hopes that the front office staff will get the prescription authorization to the doctor in a timely manner.
